(NH2)], oxytocin [(9 AAs); Cys-Tyr-Ile-Gln-Asn-Cys-Pro-Leu-Gly (NH2)], and arginine vasopressin [9 AAs; Cys-Tyr-Phe-Gln-Asn-
Cys-Pro-Arg-Gly (NH2)] (Forbes and Krishnamurthy, 2020 ). Through actions including vasoconstriction and the stimulation of
the sympathetic nervous system, angiotensin II can raise blood pressure and, therefore, is used to treat hypotension resulting
from septic shock. Bradykinin causes arterioles to dilate and augment vascular permeability by increasing the release of prostacyclin,
NO, and endothelium-derived hyperpolarizing factor from blood vessels. Oxytocin (a peptide hormone and neuropeptide)
strengthens the contractions of the uterus during labor and induces the let-down of milk from the lactating mammary glands. Argi-
nine vasopressins (also known as antidiuretic hormone) increases blood pressure in humans by stimulating the renal reabsorption
of water into the blood circulation and constricts arterioles and, therefore, is used to treat individuals with vasodilatory shock.
